summary: The optimization hypothesis was confirmed with a 54.5× speedup (1.28s → 0.023s mean runtime), far exceeding the predicted >10× improvement. All correctness tests pass, including the covering test suite and spot-checks for partition values at n=0–5, 25, 100, 200.
key_points: Baseline mean runtime: 1.2774s (std 0.0198s); optimized mean runtime: 0.0234s (std 0.0034s) — a 54.5× speedup, well above the predicted order-of-magnitude improvement.

Four synergistic optimizations were applied to the partition-counting code: (1) Dedekind sum via continued-fraction reciprocity reducing O(j) to O(log j), (2) Kloosterman sum symmetry halving iterations, (3) hardware floats for low-precision terms, and (4) gmpy2 MPFR cosine for high-precision terms.
The dominant contributor is the Dedekind sum caching/reciprocity, which eliminated an O(j²) nested loop — the core bottleneck in the _a() helper function.
All 1/1 covering tests in sympy/ntheory/tests/test_partitions.py pass; exact integer correctness verified for multiple partition values.
No surprises or regressions observed; the patch is ready for approval.
